subtitle: Lesson 19 · Visualizing Quantum States in Qiskit

caption: A measurement-outcome picture: what came out of actually running the circuit N times, nothing more.

eyebrow: Step 2: the Bloch sphere hits its real limit
titlePlain: A Maximally Mixed State Has No

steps.label: Each qubit's state is maximally mixed
steps.sub: 50/50 outcome probability, no definite phase to point to

steps.label: Geometrically: the sphere's exact center
steps.sub: Not a point on the surface — an equal mixture of every pure state

steps.label: Looks like it's showing something
steps.sub: It isn't — just the absence of any definite single-qubit state to point to

eyebrow: Step 3: the Q-sphere, where entanglement actually shows up
caption: Exactly two blobs, at 00 and 11, equal size and equal color — the real structure the Bloch sphere couldn't show.

eyebrow: Matching the picture to the audience

steps.label: Non-technical stakeholder: the histogram
steps.sub: "We ran it 1024 times, got one of two answers about half the time each" — no phase, no Hilbert space needed

steps.label: Fellow quantum engineer: the Q-sphere
steps.sub: Shows relative phase — a flipped phase with identical probabilities would look unchanged on a histogram

steps.label: The Bloch sphere is the wrong tool here
steps.sub: Reaching for it on an entangled state is itself a mistake worth being able to name
